target: Close the two unresolved, non-outdated PR #906 review threads on the DCP 0005 lane engine by hardening decide_lane against forged/restored RouteDecisions: passive lanes must drop hard-forbidden write/execute tokens via a read-only allowlist, and the executability gate must fail closed on any decision.unknowns markers. No new lane, no execution surface, no widened actions, no classifier or routing_model change.
invariants: Reachable only via a forged/restored RouteDecision; the trusted classify_route path never emits these (allowed_actions never contains _ALWAYS_FORBIDDEN tokens, and unknowns non-empty implies status is never ALLOWED).

Passive lanes (READ_ONLY_EVIDENCE, EMBEDDED_AUDIT, PR_STEWARD_READINESS, EXTERNAL_INTAKE, BLOCKED) expose only read-only/proof-safe actions; an allowlist replaces the incomplete mutating-action blocklist.
A decision carrying any unknowns marker is non-executable, mirroring the classifier invariant that unknowns implies not ALLOWED.
allowed_actions remain a subset of decision.allowed_actions; actions are only ever narrowed, never widened.
decide_lane stays a pure function with no I/O, network, shell, runner, connector, MCP, or dopetask calls.
No change to classify_route output or routing_model.py; this is lane-engine hardening only.
decide_lane has no CLI entry point, so these gaps are latent until a lane-engine consumer/executor ships; closing them now is pre-execution-surface hardening.
The deeper unforgeable-provenance contract remains DMX-DCP-MODEL-ROUTING-MVP-0007 and is out of scope here.

pr.title: fix(dcp): fail-closed lane engine on forged unknowns + hard-forbidden passive actions (PR #906 threads)
pr.body: Closes the two unresolved, non-outdated PR #906 review threads on the DCP 0005 lane engine, verified against current main. F1 (lane_engine.py:70): passive executable lanes used a mutating-action blocklist that omitted 7 classifier _ALWAYS_FORBIDDEN tokens (execute_runner, write_github_state, call_connector, execute_dopetask, mutate_task_orchestrator, run_destructive_command, touch_secrets); passive lanes now filter through a read-only allowlist. F2 (lane_engine.py:128): the executability gate never checked decision.unknowns; it now fails closed on any unknowns marker. Both are reachable only via a forged/restored RouteDecision. No new lane, no execution surface, no widened actions, no classifier or routing_model change. TDD: two regression tests verified RED before and GREEN after.

steps.task: Write failing regression tests reproducing both PR #906 findings against current-main lane engine using forged RouteDecision.from_dict fixtures.
requirements: F1 fixture: a restored READ_ONLY decision routed to the passive READ_ONLY_EVIDENCE lane while executable, carrying execute_runner and write_github_state in allowed_actions.
F2 fixture: a restored decision with all enum fields known plus unknowns=[...], status=ALLOWED, red_lane_state=CLEAR, mutating allowed_actions.
Each fixture asserts decision.is_runnable() is True so the test is not vacuous.

steps.task: Apply the two minimal fail-closed fixes in lane_engine.py.
requirements: Add bool(decision.unknowns) to _has_unknown_decision_contract so the executability gate fails closed on unknown markers.
Add a read-only allowlist filter (_read_only_safe_actions) and use it for passive lanes instead of _strip_mutating_actions.
Do not change classify_route, routing_model.py, lane KIND assignment, or add any new lane or execution path.
validation: Both new regression tests pass GREEN after the fix.
Full tests/unit/dcp/ suite passes with no regression.
ruff check clean and git diff --check clean.
